newsitem.title: UK: Pru,Fortis ready for rival bids for ScotAm--paper.
newsitem.headline: Pru,Fortis ready for rival bids for ScotAm--paper.

text.p: The Prudential and Fortis, the Belgian/Dutch insurance group, are each poised to make rival bids for Scottish Amicable, according to a report in the Sunday Telegraph newspaper.

This follows British retail banking group Abbey National's 1.4 billion stg bid for ScotAm, the life-insurance company, last week. The offer entailed a minimum of 400 million pounds to policyholders in cash or Abbey shares.

A Prudential spokesman told Reuters on Sunday he reiterated chief executive Peter Davis's comment in the paper that they were "watching the situation with interest". He declined to comment on market speculation that Pru was making a rival bid with Fortis.

On Friday, ScotAm denounced Abbey's bid as "vague" and "inadequate" and said it intended to press ahead with its two-stage plans to drop its mutual status and float the group over the next three to five years.
The Telegraph said several companies contacted ScotAm on Friday after Abbey's offer was revealed. It said National Westminster Bank and Halifax Building Society might also be interested in ScotAm.
Meanwhile The Sunday Times newspaper said the Pru had approached ScotAm with a possible bid of about 1.5 billion stg.
The newspaper said among the Continental bidders for ScotAm were Holland's ING, Germany's Allianz and France's Axa-UAP.
It said ScotAm was likely to lose its independence for almost 2.0 billion stg.

On Friday, ScotAm, which is based in Stirling, Scotland, said it intended to publish in 10 days' time detailed proposals about twin-phased transformation, involving losing its mutual status on May 1 and a 1.0 billion stg flotation in three to five years time.
